$comment: Hand-labeled from the pinned sample source (scripts/samples.json), not from Concentrate output. Spring Boot REST API with JPA, JDBC and Spring Data repositories selected by profile; labeled scope is src/main (src/test is out of scope). Routes: the REST API lives in controllers that implement interfaces (org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.api.*Api and rest.dto.*) that openapi-generator-maven-plugin generates from src/main/resources/openapi.yml at build time (pom.xml, 37 operations); neither the interfaces nor the DTOs are in the repository, so no mapping annotation of those routes is visible in the Java sources and they are a known limitation, not labeled. The only statically declared route is RootRestControllerV1's @RequestMapping(value = "/") (no method restriction, so ALL). Calls: every call site of five files whose callee is a function of this repository (and a few that must stay unresolved because the DTO class is generated): PetTypeRestControllerV1, UserRestControllerV1, UserServiceImpl, JdbcOwnerRepositoryImpl, JdbcPetVisitExtractor. A call through an interface type is labeled with the interface method and every implementing class method of the scan (ClinicService and ClinicServiceImpl; UserRepository, JdbcUserRepositoryImpl and JpaUserRepositoryImpl); MapStruct mapper interfaces (@Mapper) have no implementation in the repository (generated at build time), so the target is the interface method; a method inherited from a superclass (BaseEntity.getId, NamedEntity.setName, Pet.setType on a JdbcPet) targets the declaring class; calls on JDK, Spring and generated-DTO types are not labeled (petTypeDto.getName is labeled unresolved: PetTypeDto is generated, and Role/NamedEntity have a getName of their own). Implicit default constructors (new JdbcPetRowMapper) have no function to resolve to and are dynamic. Clinic service-to-repository calls (ClinicServiceImpl) are not labeled: a PetRepository call has up to three profile-dependent implementers. Imports: every import of every Java file under src/main/java, resolved by qualified name to the .java file of the repository; wildcard imports and imports of JDK, third-party and generated (rest.api, rest.dto) types are target null. Injections: Spring beans in src/main/java. Constructor injection of ClinicService/UserService (one implementation: ClinicServiceImpl, UserServiceImpl) into the nine controllers; ClinicServiceImpl's constructor, UserServiceImpl's @Autowired field and JdbcPetRepositoryImpl's constructor receive a repository interface whose @Repository implementations are chosen by @Profile (jdbc, jpa; spring-data-jpa repositories are interfaces proxied by Spring Data, not classes), so every concrete implementer class in the same configuration is a candidate edge (JdbcPetRepositoryImpl is profile jdbc, so only JdbcOwnerRepositoryImpl). Mapper parameters get no edge: the MapStruct implementations are generated. Data access: direct accesses in the repository implementation classes of the Owner, PetType, Specialty, User, Pet and Visit entities (jdbc/, jpa/, springdatajpa/*Impl). Model is the table for raw SQL (JdbcTemplate) and the entity class for JPA (EntityManager find/createQuery/persist/merge/remove); persist is create; merge is upsert (it inserts or updates); a merge that only re-attaches an entity before em.remove (delete methods) writes nothing and is not labeled. A COUNT query is an aggregate (JPQL and JDBC alike). A join fetch / JOIN also reads the joined table. SimpleJdbcInsert is configured with withTableName in the constructor but inserts in save (executeAndReturnKey / execute). Overloads of one name are one function. Spring Data repository interfaces declare queries without a body and are not labeled. Env: the ${NAME:default} placeholders of the profile properties files that Spring resolves from the process environment (POSTGRES_*, MYSQL_*); ${spring.sql.init.platform} refers to another property and is not an environment variable. SQL tables are not labeled: the db/<vendor>/schema.sql files are plain schema files, not migrations, and the scan merges their nine tables into the JPA entities, so the harness scores them as Tables declared in model/*.java with the entity's Java column types (Integer, String), not the DDL.
